measured_from: 12 completed push runs of Tests, 38094792310..38170451554, read on 2026-10-11: 132 job records, 132 that ran, 0 cancelled by a later push
notes: budget_seconds is compared against the p90 of the step, nearest-rank, over the runs read.

A budget exists only for a step that ran on a push: the pull-request-only install step is absent here on purpose, because declaring it would make the leg red every night for a step that cannot run outside a PR.

Serial gates carry their own budget because they run alone in their step: see tests/test_timing_assertion_guard.py and the owner rule that a wall-clock budget never absorbs contention from a parallel sibling.
The p90 figures in measured_p90_seconds were read from the Actions API on 2026-10-11; a budget is raised or lowered by measuring again, never to make a red go away.

The wall-clock startup gate is a local-only instrument, so it is absent from entries by design: its budget is one machine's p50 and no percentile absorbs a shared runner, so tests/test_bench_gates.py skips it on CI (_LOCAL_BASELINE_ONLY) and tests/test_cli_dx.py::test_cli_keeps_heavy_imports_lazy is the CI-enforceable form. Locally it stands down under load via tests/timing_segment.py (xdist worker, or >= 2.0 runnable tasks per CPU); a red on a loaded box is re-run on an idle box before it counts.
